newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends up in thin and rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends up in thin and rangebound trade.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled slightly firmer on speculative buying, but trade selling at the highs prevented the most-active May contract from reaching its overhead target, dealers said.
May closed 0.07 cent higher at 75.22 cents per pound, traded 75.50 to 75.15 cents. Spot-March ended 0.10 cent higher at 73.20 cents, and the outer months settled unchanged to up 0.25.
Volume was estimated at 8,500 lots compared with Friday's official volume of 20,740 lots.
Open interest in May rose 1,593 lots to 35,555 lots.
Prices are expected to remain within their recent trading range amid a lack of news.
Players await the speculator/hedge report issued by the New York Cotton Exchange on Tuesday, and the weekly export and sales report issued by the U.S. Department of Agriculture on Thursday.
